evidence.title: Reframed a roadmap of separate enhancements into one product direction
evidence.contribution: The Agent Portal roadmap listed individual enhancements: TC access, order status improvements, dashboard and quick actions, and an enhanced order journey. Sarah identified that they could form one cohesive experience and positioned the work as a unified 3.0 redesign.
evidence.outcome: Separate enhancements were connected into a redesign of the portal's core workflows (design direction; development is underway, no post-launch results yet).

source.label: UX Case Study - HW Agent Portal - Redesign Overview.pdf

evidence.title: Aligned stakeholders through journey mapping and rapid prototyping
evidence.contribution: Reviewed TC research, workflows and planned enhancements; reviewed competitor portals; collaborated with stakeholders to uncover requirements; built a working Magic Patterns prototype combining the dashboard, order management and order creation to gain alignment before testing with TCs. Participated in the Atlanta stakeholder workshop.
evidence.outcome: The prototype accelerated stakeholder collaboration, uncovered new requirements and established a shared direction.

source.label: UX Case Study - HW Agent Portal - Redesign Overview.pdf

verification.note: Atlanta workshop participation is from the project brief; the case study does not mention it.

evidence.title: Validated the prototype with six transaction coordinators
evidence.contribution: Ran follow-up sessions with six TCs on the rapid prototype and synthesized the feedback into an updated product direction.
evidence.outcome: TCs described the prototype as simple, intuitive and easier than today's process. Validated areas: overall workflow, agent selection placement, quote-to-order progression, dashboard cards that surface exceptions, the Orders page as a one-stop shop, and plan and pricing transparency. Opportunities noted: claim initiation (a subset of TCs, a later expansion), role-dependent expired/cancelled visibility, and optional agent fields. This is pre-launch prototype feedback, not post-launch performance.

source.label: TC Prototype Results.docx; UX Case Study - HW Agent Portal - Redesign Overview.pdf

evidence.title: Owned detailed end-to-end design for development handoff
evidence.contribution: Solved workflows, business rules and edge cases beyond the prototype: listing coverage activation states, agent search and addition (including agents not in the system), property address search within Google API constraints, quote and invoice sharing, flexible payer selection and payment collection, and empty, loading, error and confirmation states with microcopy. The brief also lists plan selection, order management and responsive mobile states.
evidence.outcome: Redesigned experience prepared for development handoff (case study lists handoff as almost done; implementation underway).

source.label: UX Case Study - HW Agent Portal - Redesign Overview.pdf

verification.note: Plan selection, order management and mobile states come from the brief; confirm against the Figma files.

evidence.title: Dashboard redesigned to show what needs attention at a glance
evidence.contribution: Redesigned the dashboard from reviewing individual orders to surfacing priorities such as upcoming closings and action-needed items.
evidence.outcome: Design change shown as before/after in the case study. TCs specifically valued 'closing soon' and 'payment attention needed' cards in prototype sessions (pre-launch feedback).

source.label: UX Case Study - HW Agent Portal - Redesign Overview.pdf; TC Prototype Results.docx

evidence.title: Orders redesigned for centralized management, search, filtering and closing-date prioritization
evidence.contribution: Designed centralized order management across multiple agents with clear statuses, search by property address, assigned agent or outstanding action, and closing-date prioritization. These address known pain points: no filtering or robust search, difficulty locating orders, and no closing-date prioritization.
evidence.outcome: Design change shown before/after in the case study. TCs liked the filters, agent filter and one-stop layout in the prototype (pre-launch feedback).

source.label: UX Case Study - HW Agent Portal - Redesign Overview.pdf; TC Prototype Results.docx

evidence.title: Section-based create and edit flow replacing linear navigation
evidence.contribution: Designed one experience for creating and editing orders, with sections that can be completed as information becomes available and clear progress and requirements. Addresses prior pain points: no stepper, long order creation, and editing that required contacting support.
evidence.outcome: Design change shown before/after in the case study; not yet measured post-launch.

source.label: UX Case Study - HW Agent Portal - Redesign Overview.pdf

evidence.title: Analyzed how users add devices: category browsing versus type-ahead search
evidence.contribution: Reviewed 30 days of one-session data for mobile-only clients and analyzed why category selection was preferred, then recommended a design change to make search equally apparent. Analysis and recommendations were created before AI was used to review the data.
evidence.outcome: Baseline observations (not post-change gains): 71% chose category selection and 17% chose type-ahead search when adding a device. Of those who chose each method, 74% saved a device via type-ahead search and 52% via category selection. Conclusion: update the design so search has similar hierarchy to browse by category, then monitor the live change.

source.label: UX Case Study - Adding Devices- North Star.pdf

verification.note: Scope: 30 days, one-session data, mobile-only clients. Not a post-change result.

evidence.title: Improved the Getting Started add-devices flow with peer review and Figma Make
evidence.contribution: Edited the add-device flow in the Getting Started journey to give immediate feedback, allow for user error, and give a clear path to add multiple devices and finish. Took the idea to peer review, used Figma Make to generate concepts, and reviewed top versus bottom bar options in peer review. The final flow solves for a user who leaves without adding a device.
evidence.outcome: Final flow designed. Planned measures: devices added within the flow and drop-off rate. No results reported yet, so this is design intent.

source.label: UX Case Study - Adding Devices- North Star.pdf

verification.note: Success measures are planned, not reported.
